The core activating feature is a distinct vertical line, bar, or shadow—such as a dark dorsal stripe on an animal, a harness strap, a fabric seam, an instrument needle, or a vertical crevice—rendered in **deep charcoal or black** against a **lighter, desaturated background** of light grey, medium grey, or off-white. This feature creates a sharp dark-on-light contrast and consistently follows the vertical axis of the composition. The neuron remains invariant to object identity (responding to insects, mammals, machinery, and abstract shadows alike), surface texture, and lighting direction, provided the vertical geometry and tonal contrast are preserved. Quantitatively, the activating vertical element typically occupies 40–90% of the image height and is positioned centrally or slightly off-center within the frame.
